'''Cathy Kessel''' is a U.S. researcher in mathematics education<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/viaf-164510248/ |title=Kessel, Cathy |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=November 6, 2016}}</ref> and consultant, past-president of [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], winner of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] [[Louise Hay Award]], and a blogger on Mathematics and Education.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathedck.wordpress.com/|title=Mathematics and Education|website=Mathematics and Education|language=en-US|access-date=2016-11-05}}</ref> She served as an editor for ''Illustrative Mathematics'' from the end of 2015 through July 15, 2017.<ref>[https://www.illustrativemathematics.org Illustrative Mathematics]</ref>

== Biography ==
Kessel received her Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Colorado Boulder]], specializing in [[mathematical logic]], and taught for three years after earning her Ph.D. She taught for a total of 13 years as a graduate and postgraduate until the 1990s when she made the switch to research in education.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathedck.files.wordpress.com/2010/03/kessel-ume-trends-article-1990.pdf|title=Why I Quit My Job|last=Kessel|first=Cathy|date=|website=|publisher=|access-date=}}</ref> She began auditing courses and working on research projects at the School of Education at the [[University of California at Berkeley]]. This led to a career that included editing reports, books, articles, and curriculum and standards documents. She was the president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from 2007 to 2009 and worked as a mathematics education consultant through 2015 and again after she left Illustrative Mathematics in 2017.

== Projects ==
Kessel has participated in multiple projects pertaining to mathematics education, including the following.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://mathedck.wordpress.com/about-this-blogger/|title=About this blogger|date=2010-03-09|newspaper=Mathematics and Education|language=en-US|access-date=2016-11-05}}</ref>
* Editor and indexer, Liping Ma, ''Knowing and Teaching Elementary Mathematics'', first edition, Lawrence Erlbaum Associates, 1999; anniversary edition, Routledge, 2010
* Additional writer, ''Principles and Standards of School Mathematics'', National Council of Teachers of Mathematics, 2000
* Editor, ''Mathematical Education of Teachers'', Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences, 2001
* Consultant, Research for Better Schools guide to TIMSS public release videos, 2005
* Writer, ''Learning Across Boundaries: U.S.–Japan Collaboration in Mathematics, Science and Technology Education'', 2007<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lessonresearch.net/LOB1.pdf|title=Learning Across Boundaries PDF|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317174849/http://lessonresearch.net/LOB1.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-17|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Editor, Critical Issues in Mathematics Education workshop booklet, ''Teaching Teachers Mathematics: Research, Ideas, Projects, Evaluation'', Mathematical Sciences Research Institute, 2009
* Editor, ''Mathematical Education of Teachers II'', Conference Board of the Mathematical Sciences, 2012<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbmsweb.org/MET2/index.htm|title=MET2|website=www.cbmsweb.org|access-date=2016-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026201529/http://www.cbmsweb.org/MET2/index.htm|archive-date=2016-10-26|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Writer, ''Mathematics Curriculum, Teacher Professionalism, and Supporting Policies in Korea and the United States: Summary of a Workshop'', 2015, National Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite book|last=Medicine|first=National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and|date=2015-10-07|title=Mathematics Curriculum, Teacher Professionalism, and Supporting Policies in Korea and the United States: Summary of a Workshop|url=https://www.nap.edu/catalog/21753/mathematics-curriculum-teacher-professionalism-and-supporting-policies-in-korea-and-the-united-states|doi=10.17226/21753|isbn=978-0-309-37436-1}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] twenty-seventh annual [[Louise Hay Award]] (January 2017)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/hay-award/hay-award-2017|title=Louise Hay Award-2017 Winner:Cathy Kessel|website=awm-math.org|access-date=2021-01-13}}</ref>

In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|website=awm-math.org|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=9 January 2021}}</ref>
